messages:
Marisa: Hey team — heads up i need to do a split-week arrangement: live in SF but planning to spend ~3 days/week in Guadalajara for family starting May. curious about: payroll/homebase, WFH stipend proration, benefits impact, and whether we need to register payroll in Mexico if this continues. low-stress timeline (aiming to start May 18).
Jamal (People Ops): Thanks for the heads up, Marisa. A few quick Qs: are you keeping your US lease + bank account? will you be on the Mexican visa or tourist? those details change the advice.
Marisa: Keeping SF lease and US bank. No visa yet — likely tourist initially. travel pattern is repeat weekly (Mon-Wed MX, Thu-Fri SF).
Jamal (People Ops): OK. Two main things: 1) homebase rules — if you maintain US primary residence and <183 days in MX per rolling 12mo you typically stay on US payroll/benefits. 2) stipend/proration — we pro-rate monthly WFH allowance by days away from homebase. I'll confirm exact proration calc.
Emma (Payroll): hi Marisa — Payroll here. If you're under US payroll we continue standard deductions. For stipend: we split by calendar days in the month (company policy). Example: if 9/30 days in MX we pro-rate accordingly. Need exact dates to run scenarios.
tax_counsel: quick note from tax side: 183-day rule is a common threshold for tax residency but local law + employer presence can create nexus earlier. repeating weekly pattern can raise employer withholding obligations in Mexico if local authorities view it as habitual work there. recommend limiting to <183 days and tracking days precisely. we should review if customers or server activity creates PE risk.
Marisa: Got it. Tracking days will be manual at first — can HR recommend a tracker?
luis (People Ops): hr-bot has a mobility tracker we use for pilots. @hr-bot please drop the form.
hr-bot: Mobility form generated: https://redwood.internal/hr/mobility-form?request=2712345678 — fill travel dates + visa status + laptop location.
Jamal (People Ops): Please complete that form. After submission we'll: (a) evaluate benefits eligibility (health, commuter), (b) calculate stipend proration for first month, (c) loop in legal if MX days approach threshold.
Emma (Payroll): Also confirm whether you'll need payroll in MX. If you exceed thresholds or local authorities ask, we may need to run local payroll or use a payroll partner. That can take 4–6 weeks to set up — flagging early.
Marisa: If we go the contractor route for the MX days would that be easier?
tax_counsel: Short-term contractor arrangements can avoid employer payroll in some cases but have tradeoffs: classification risk, local labor rules, and benefits gaps. For recurring work pattern it's not a simple mitigation. We'll chat if you prefer that route.
Marisa: Understood. For equipment: i need to ship my dock and monitor to MX for those days. Does Redwood cover cross-border shipping?
Jamal (People Ops): Yes we can cover shipping for approved equipment. Submit a ticket via the Equipment portal and attach the mobility form. Shipping costs are reimbursed up to policy limits.
Marisa: cool — will fill the form tonight. any docs I should read first?
luis (People Ops): Read: https://redwood.internal/policies/homebase-and-remote (homebase rules) and the Mexico note in the tax KB: https://redwood.internal/kb/tax/mexico-guidance.
Emma (Payroll): Action for payroll once form submitted: we'll run sample paycheck scenarios for May and June and DM results.
Jamal (People Ops): Next steps for Marisa: 1) complete mobility form, 2) attach planned dates + shipping ticket, 3) we'll schedule a 15-min sync with Payroll + Legal if needed. Thanks! :thumbsup:
